open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes input boundary
open_points.text: “One JSON value” and “refuse a value JCS cannot represent: a non-finite number, a duplicate key”; also “module:surface turns every JSON text a request carries … into its canonical form with canonical_values.canonical_bytes”
open_points.question: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text and parse it so duplicate keys remain detectable, or does surface parse first and reject duplicate keys before passing a value?
options: canonical_bytes accepts raw JSON text and owns parsing
surface uses a duplicate-preserving/rejecting parser before passing a parsed value
duplicate members are collapsed by parsing
open_points.default_guess: Have canonical_bytes accept raw JSON text and own duplicate-key detection.

open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case port coverage
open_points.text: “input values by port, optional expected outputs” and “Fit in port name order — presence, carriage, schema, size”
open_points.question: Must inputs contain exactly every input port and no extra names, and when expected_outputs is present must it contain exactly every output port, or may expected outputs be partial?
options: exact input set; expected outputs either absent or the exact output set
exact input set; expected outputs may be a subset
missing ports are refused but extra names are ignored
open_points.default_guess: Require the exact input set and require expected outputs, when present, to contain the exact output set.

open_points.subject: effects.decide_effect_approval refusal trace
open_points.text: Inputs are only “An approval identity, approve or refuse, the actor …; from runs that the run has not ended”, but refusal writes “the element's NodeExecution refused_by_owner”; M23 requires that NodeExecution to name its inputs as StoredValue and SpooledFile references.
open_points.question: Where does decide_effect_approval obtain the exact input references required for the refused_by_owner NodeExecution?
options: runs passes the element's input references into decide_effect_approval
EffectApproval stores the full input references, not only input_digests and preview
effects reconstructs the inputs from run records
open_points.default_guess: Pass the element's input references from runs into decide_effect_approval.

open_points.subject: operation failure diagnostics in NodeExecution
open_points.text: send_prepared_request returns “for operation_failed its detail code … and a bounded failure_detail”, while M23 provides only one field, “failure_detail”; State 5 separately says operation_failed details are a closed code set.
open_points.question: How are both the machine-actionable operation-failure code and a response-body diagnostic represented and persisted, especially for a read answered 3xx?
options: store separate failure_code and bounded failure_detail fields
encode both into the single failure_detail field with a fixed structure
keep only the closed failure code
keep only the response-body diagnostic
open_points.default_guess: Store a separate closed failure_code alongside the bounded diagnostic failure_detail.

open_points.subject: approval request digest for multipart requests
open_points.text: State 0 says approval covers “the fully built request … headers and body” and “Any difference at send … asks again”; A10 says the multipart content type is described “without its boundary parameter” and “the boundary is not part of it”.
open_points.question: Does a changed multipart boundary invalidate an approval, and how is content-length determined when the boundary that affects the wire body length is excluded from the approved request description?
options: use a deterministic boundary and include it and the resulting content-length in approval coverage
exclude the boundary and define approvals over semantic multipart parts rather than exact wire bytes
exclude the boundary but require its encoded length to remain unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Follow the later specific rule: exclude the boundary and define approval coverage over the ordered multipart parts, with content-length derived from the actual encoding.

open_points.subject: service api_base_url grammar and joining
open_points.text: A base URL need only be “an absolute http or https URL with a host”, while the request URL is “the api_base_url without a trailing / followed by the declared path” and “Nothing else is normalized.”
open_points.question: Are a base URL's userinfo, query, fragment and path prefix allowed, and is joining literal concatenation or URL-component resolution?
options: permit only scheme, host, optional port and an optional path prefix; forbid userinfo, query and fragment
allow every absolute URL and concatenate strings literally
allow every absolute URL and resolve the declared path using URL-resolution rules
open_points.default_guess: Allow an optional path prefix but forbid userinfo, query and fragment, then join by the specified slash rule.

open_points.subject: store.spool_file ceiling refusal cleanup
open_points.text: A ceiling refusal keeps “nothing … of that file or of any file that attempt spooled before”, although those earlier files were published by separate spool_file calls; an I/O failure is internal_error only “with nothing kept of that file”.
open_points.question: What happens if removing an earlier file of the same attempt fails while handling a ceiling refusal, and what result and spool accounting must the operation expose?
options: return internal_error and retain any undeleted files as unnamed, counted spool bytes
return refused even if physical cleanup fails and exclude leftovers from logical accounting
make all files of an attempt one atomic spool operation
open_points.default_guess: Return internal_error if cleanup cannot be completed, leaving any physical remnants unnamed but explicitly accounted for until run-spool removal.

open_points.subject: masked failure_detail length
open_points.text: “A failure_detail of an execution whose class is above open is returned to an agent only as its length and that class.”
open_points.question: What unit is the disclosed length: UTF-8 bytes before truncation, UTF-8 bytes after truncation, Unicode code points, or another measure?
options: UTF-8 byte length of the stored bounded detail
Unicode code-point count of the stored detail
original pre-truncation UTF-8 byte length
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, already bounded failure_detail.
